title: Types and missing values
explanation: Every value in R has a **type**: numbers are **numeric**, text is **character**, and TRUE/FALSE is **logical**. Real data also has gaps. R marks a missing value as **NA** (not available), and NA changes how functions behave. Two games in the `games` table have no rating.

tasks.teach: **class()** tells you the type. Columns of text are "character", and columns of numbers are "numeric" (or "integer" for whole numbers).
tasks.prompt: Check the type of the title column with class(), and store it in col_type.
hints: class() tells you a value's type.

tasks.teach: `==` compares, and gives back **TRUE** or **FALSE** for every value. A single `=` doesn't compare.
tasks.prompt: Make a TRUE/FALSE vector of which prices are 0 (free games): free <- games$price == 0.
Count the free games: sum() counts TRUEs, because TRUE counts as 1. Store it in n_free.
hints: sum() of a TRUE/FALSE vector counts the TRUEs.

tasks.teach: If any value is **NA**, the mean is NA too, because R can't know the missing values. R does this on purpose, so you notice the gaps.
tasks.prompt: Try the average rating: run mean(games$rating) and see what happens.
hints: It gives NA, because 2 ratings are missing. That's expected!

tasks.teach: **na.rm = TRUE** means "NA remove: skip the missing values". Most summary functions accept it: sum(), max(), min() and more.
tasks.prompt: Last one: tell mean() to skip the missing values with na.rm = TRUE, and store the result in avg_rating.
hints: Add na.rm = TRUE inside mean(), after a comma.

recap: Values are numeric, character or logical, and class() tells you which. == compares and gives TRUE/FALSE, and sum() counts TRUEs. NA marks missing data, and na.rm = TRUE skips it.
